newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia plans cellular phone quality index.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia plans cellular phone quality index.

text.p: Malaysia's Department of Telecommunications said on Monday it was preparing a benchmark to measure the quality of cellular phone services.

The department, Jabatan Telekom Malaysia (JTM), Director General Hod Parman said the department has recently completed a study of the eight celluar telephone services in the country to collect data for the planned index.
"Analysis of the data will contribute towards setting the service quality index," Hod said at a ceremony to mark 10 years of privatisation of telecommunication services in Malaysia.
He said JTM was also working with the opertors to streamline industry regulations.
"(The move) will involve revision to the method of payment or tariffs based on cost. This will also involve determining the regulations on carrying out the universal service agreement," said Hod.
Under the government's unversal services obligation, new fixed line telephone operators will also have to provide services to outlying areas.
The government-run Telekom Malaysia Bhd is the only operator providing fixed-line services to rural areas which are less profitable than urban areas.
